claim_boundary: This is a descriptive review of one frozen project case by three judges. It reports no confidence interval, p-value, population generalization, provider usage, cost efficiency, or causal architecture superiority.

repairs: Using development-only data, freeze strata from cue-visible, non-outcome covariates; specify bin edges or matcher, distinct-patient minimums, handling of sparse cells and missingness, and whether strata affect sampling or analysis. Bind the definition before held-out access and hard-stop if no adequately supported ambiguity stratum remains.

Using development-only data, prospectively define the cue-visible covariates, deterministic bins or matching rule, per-stratum distinct-patient support threshold, handling of unsupported and missing strata, whether strata affect sampling or analysis, and their multiplicity status; hash this contract before held-out access.

Using development/validation data only, freeze cue-visible covariates, binning or matching algorithm, distinct-patient support thresholds, unsupported-stratum handling, whether strata affect sampling or analysis, and the exact stratum-specific estimands before test access.
summaries: Y makes cue-matched ambiguity strata load-bearing for the distinguishing signal and stronger falsifier, but leaves their covariates, definitions, support thresholds and sampling-versus-analysis role open. This permits a later choice of strata that either removes difficult anatomy or exposes target/scope through cue morphology.

Y makes adequately supported cue-matched ambiguity strata central to mechanistic interpretation while explicitly leaving their definitions, covariates, support thresholds and sampling-versus-analysis role open.
Y makes cue-matched ambiguity strata load-bearing for mechanism discrimination but leaves their covariates, definitions, support thresholds, and analysis-versus-sampling use unresolved.

repairs: Choose one shared schedule using development-only evidence, freeze patient sampling, joint weighting, stage transitions, minibatch order, update count and stopping behavior in the F0 manifest, and restrict any staged-versus-flat comparison to a separately registered development audit.

Choose the schedule using development-only evidence, then freeze and hash the same patient sampler, stage or flat policy, minibatch order, update count, optimizer, stopping rule, seed list and checkpoint-selection procedure for both arms; keep any schedule comparison separately registered and non-rescuing.

Choose and hash one shared patient-first or flat schedule before fitting, including sampler, minibatch order, seed mapping, update budget, stopping, and checkpoint selection; keep any staged-versus-flat comparison as a separate development-only audit.
summaries: Y requires a shared full/no_M0 schedule but leaves staged patient-first curriculum versus a flat sampler unresolved. Because schedule and exposure can interact with joint rarity and anatomical difficulty, the primary training intervention is not yet exactly reproducible.

Y does not choose between staged and flat training even though a shared schedule and identical exposure are necessary to prevent optimization differences from confounding the full-versus-no_M0 contrast.
Y leaves staged versus flat training unresolved even though a shared exposure schedule is required to interpret full versus no_M0 as an access-only contrast.

repairs: Before fitting, sign an exhaustive A_M0 manifest with one rule for every direct and derived path, including state-support pooling, caches, normalization, filenames and missingness; freeze neutral values in the normalized space and require byte-level non-M0 parity, paired tensor-diff checks and the stated M0-swap invariance test.

Close an F0-signed exhaustive M0-path allowlist and specify the exact normalized-space neutral value or masking operation for every channel, support, pooled feature, geometry field, cache and metadata path; preserve shapes and non-M0 bytes, then require byte-level tensor-diff and M0-perturbation invariance tests before training.

Freeze the exhaustive direct-and-derived M0 path allowlist and, for every path, the normalized-space neutral value or masking/removal rule, state-support behavior, geometry handling, normalization source, parameter-opportunity policy, and byte-level metamorphic and tensor-diff acceptance tests.
summaries: Y leaves the path-wise no_M0 neutralization rule open even though that intervention defines the primary mechanistic contrast. Zeroing, masking, removal and replacement can change scale, missingness, support pooling or effective capacity differently and can themselves reveal arm identity.

Y requires exhaustive no_M0 removal but leaves each direct and derived M0 path's neutralization, state-support behavior, normalized scale and parameter-opportunity treatment unresolved, so the defining intervention is not reproducible or demonstrably isolated.
Y requires exhaustive M0 removal but leaves the path-wise neutralization rule open, so the intervention and its scale, missingness, capacity, and optimization parity are not yet reproducible.
